parsed.rationale: Although `PlaybackController` and `TimeShiftablePlayer` share four members (`installRenderTap:()`, `removeRenderTap:()`, `isPlaying:Bool`, `makeAudioBufferStream:() -> AsyncStream<AVAudioPCMBuffer>`), the structural evidence reports `shared_field_count: 0` and `jaccard: null`, indicating the pipeline itself found no meaningful overlap. More importantly, the two protocols encode distinct domain responsibilities: `PlaybackController` models high-level playback control with `PlaybackState`, `PlaybackReason`, and `toggle`, while `TimeShiftablePlayer` models a time-shifting audio player with `seek`, `seekToLive`, `secondsBehindLive`, `maxLookbackSeconds`, `stateStream`, and `timePositionStream`. Forcing a parent protocol would either over-constrain `PlaybackController` conformers with time-shift semantics they don't need, or produce a vacuously thin base that adds no real abstraction. The coincidence of a handful of tap-management and stream methods is structural only; the domain concepts are genuinely divergent.
